hypothesis: monthly SIP debit concentration moves the index enough to trade
endpoint: max single-date SIP flow / NSE cash turnover -> square-root price impact vs 3x delivery floor
verdict: PRECHECK_NOT_CLOSED: largest implied move 123.23 bps (Dec-2025, SIP Rs 31,002 cr, Q/V 0.328) vs the 71.35 bps bar; median 109.55 bps; 27 of 27 months clear. Survives the un-generous reading too -- 82.15 bps at the consensus Y=1.0, break-even Y 0.869. TWO LOAD-BEARING CAVEATS: it rests on MAX CONCENTRATION (whole month on one date; spread over the ~7 usual debit dates the largest month gives ~47 bps, BELOW the bar), and on EXTRAPOLATION -- Q/V runs 0.139-0.328 against a square-root law calibrated on metaorders of a few percent of daily volume. NOT CLOSED means the arithmetic does not rule it out, NOT that an edge exists. Window 2024-06..2026-08 only; AMFI publishes no machine-readable monthly SIP series before the June-2024 note, so the median is NOT since 2016.

hypothesis: SIP debits on the 10th move the index over D..D+2
endpoint: month-clustered SIP-day vs other-day difference in the 3-session NIFTY 500 return vs 3x the NIFTY futures statutory floor
verdict: GATE_CLOSED_UNDERPOWERED: MDE 53.20 bps vs the 16.9664 bps futures bar (3.14x). Non-overlapping comparison group (excluding the D-2..D+2 starts) gives 53.93 bps, so the verdict does not depend on which comparison group is used. In TRUE-EFFECT terms the MDE is 59.12 bps (3.48x), because a real effect leaks into the overlapping comparison windows and the measured difference is only 0.900 of it -- closed form 1-(L-1)/m_other, checked by simulation in ARM 8. Clearing the bar at this volatility would need ~1,268 months (~106 years). Dose-response DROPPED: only two fiscal years of official AMFI SIP totals exist. 42 of 129 events moved forward off a non-trading 10th. The pre-check's spread-concentration estimate (~47 bps) sits BELOW this detection floor, so the two phases agree.
